how_exchange_rates_work.heading: How exchange rates work
paragraphs: An exchange rate shows how much one currency is worth in terms of another. These values change as markets respond to inflation, interest rates, trade flows, growth expectations, and geopolitical developments.
The rate shown on ConvertCCY is intended as a reference point for comparison. It can help users estimate relative currency value before dealing with bank, card, or transfer-provider pricing.

trust_block.heading: Reference, not markup
trust_block.text: ConvertCCY is built to highlight the market relationship between currencies as clearly as possible. Customer-facing exchange rates can differ because financial institutions often apply spread, margin, or service fees.

mid_market_section.heading: Reference rate vs bank rate
paragraphs: The reference exchange rate is useful because it shows the market relationship between two currencies without adding a customer-specific fee structure.
Banks, cards, travel desks, and money-transfer providers often apply a spread or markup on top of the market relationship, so the final customer rate can be less favorable.

exchange_rate_explained.heading: What an exchange rate means
paragraphs: An exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in another currency. In simple terms, it shows how much of one unit is needed to buy a unit of another.
Exchange rates can move because financial markets constantly reassess value using information such as inflation, economic growth, trade conditions, interest-rate policy, and risk sentiment.

mid_market_explained.heading: What the mid-market or reference rate means
paragraphs: A reference exchange rate is used as a neutral comparison point between two currencies. It helps users evaluate relative value without immediately folding in card fees, transfer margins, or travel desk spreads.
This makes a reference rate especially useful for planning, research, budgeting, and checking whether a quoted customer rate appears competitive.

bank_rate_explained.heading: Why bank and provider rates can differ
paragraphs: Retail exchange pricing often includes a margin above the market relationship between two currencies. That difference can appear as a spread, conversion fee, or less favorable quoted rate.
This is why the rate displayed by a bank, money-transfer service, or travel exchange counter may differ from a neutral reference rate.

market_drivers_explained.heading: What moves currencies
paragraphs: Currencies are influenced by interest rates, inflation, central-bank policy, trade balances, capital flows, and broader investor sentiment.
Some currencies are also sensitive to commodities, geopolitical events, or safe-haven demand during periods of global uncertainty.

faq_defaults.a: This page shows the latest available reference exchange rate for converting {FROM_NAME} to {TO_NAME}.
Exchange rates change as markets respond to inflation, interest rates, growth expectations, trade conditions, and overall market sentiment.

faq_defaults.q: Is this the same as a bank rate?
faq_defaults.a: Not always. Banks and financial providers often apply a spread or fee, which can make the customer-facing rate different from a reference market rate.

faq_defaults.q: What affects the value of {FROM_CODE} against {TO_CODE}?
faq_defaults.a: This pair can be influenced by central-bank policy, inflation, growth conditions, trade flows, and broad risk appetite in financial markets.

remittance.q: Why is this pair useful for transfers and remittances?
remittance.a: Some currency pairs are searched frequently because they are widely used for household transfers, travel, work-related payments, and cross-border support.

major_major.q: Why is this considered an important currency pair?
major_major.a: Pairs made up of widely traded currencies often become benchmark references in market commentary, pricing, hedging, and international comparisons.

commodity_sensitive.q: Can commodity prices affect this pair?
commodity_sensitive.a: Yes. Some currencies can be influenced by commodity-linked export revenue, trade conditions, and changes in global demand.

safe_haven_linked.q: Can market stress affect this pair more sharply?
safe_haven_linked.a: Yes. When either side of the pair has safe-haven characteristics, changes in global risk sentiment can play a larger role in price movement.

about.title: About ConvertCCY
about.intro: ConvertCCY is an independent digital platform designed to make currency value easier to understand across borders, markets, and everyday financial decisions.
paragraphs: Currency conversion is often presented only as a number, but the meaning behind that number matters. ConvertCCY is built to provide both a practical reference tool and a growing layer of explanation around exchange rates, relative value, and the forces that shape currency pricing.

The platform focuses on reference-first comparison. It is intended to help users understand how currencies relate to one another, while also recognizing that banks and payment providers may quote different customer rates.
Over time, ConvertCCY is intended to grow into a broader reference resource for currency knowledge, market context, and practical exchange-rate understanding.

methodology.title: Methodology
paragraphs: ConvertCCY uses reference-rate logic to present the relative market value between currency pairs for informational comparison.
Exchange-rate displays on the platform should be treated as reference indicators rather than a guarantee of retail execution pricing.
Rates shown by banks, card issuers, travel desks, or transfer services can differ due to spread, markup, timing, or service fees.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
paragraphs: ConvertCCY provides informational reference content only and does not provide financial, investment, tax, legal, or transfer advice.
Users should verify actual pricing directly with financial institutions or service providers before making a transaction or relying on a quoted customer rate.

footer_copy.line_1: ConvertCCY provides reference exchange-rate content for informational comparison.
footer_copy.line_2: Customer pricing from banks, cards, and transfer providers may differ.
